bull.b: The 191 MW, 20-year lease adds substantial contracted revenue beyond bitcoin mining and supports a more durable infrastructure model. Its projected high NOI margin could improve earnings quality as capacity is delivered, while the long tenor provides visibility for capital planning and expansion.

Strong engineering growth, expanding gross margin, and a sizeable data-center-heavy backlog indicate useful internal capabilities supporting Riot’s infrastructure transition. This vertical integration may improve execution and shorten equipment lead times as contracted deployments scale over the next several quarters.

Low power costs are a durable operating advantage in bitcoin mining, where electricity is a core input and network competition can pressure unit economics. Riot’s reported efficiency can help protect contribution margins, support uptime and preserve flexibility through changing mining conditions.

bear.b: Severe losses and persistent cash consumption weaken internal funding capacity and reduce confidence in near-term capital efficiency. Unless profitability improves, Riot may need to keep selling assets, raising financing, or redirecting resources, limiting flexibility while it expands its data-center platform.

bear.t: High capital intensity and financing reliance
bear.b: Riot’s growth plan requires substantial upfront investment before the contracted facilities are fully delivered, creating execution and funding demands over multiple years. Reliance on project financing, interim debt and capital recycling could constrain returns or increase financial pressure if delivery or financing assumptions change.

Bitcoin mining remains a core revenue source, so operating results can remain structurally volatile even as data-center contracts grow. Changes in bitcoin economics, network competition or power costs can compress mining profitability and make consolidated earnings and cash generation less predictable.
